surface_mechanism_description: The growth process involves alternating deposition of Cd and Te2 molecules on the (111)B surface of a CdTe substrate. The chemisorbed atoms form a relatively stable surface with a low vapor pressure at the growth temperature. The outermost Cd cover layer is weakly bonded to the Te layer underneath, and the bulk-like termination for the film is obtained only if the deposition is ended with a Te2 pulse on the (111)B substrate. The mechanism of epitaxial monoatomic layer-by-layer growth via surface reactions on an ideal CdTe (111) substrate is slightly different from growth of non-polar (110) films, where Cd and Te are situated coplanary.
